Real result (llama3.2:latest, 2026-09-18): parsing fidelity 8/16 (50%) against the corpus author's own asserted_object (a golden check never read by the evidence-building code path, verified by test_perfect_parser_reproduces_the_corpus_authors_intended_diversity); of 14 candidates, 7 records produced (5 SUPPORTED, 2 CONTRADICTED -- genuine outcome diversity, unlike the closed-question mechanism's degenerate 16/16 CONTRADICTED), 3 excluded_no_matching_text_claim (ENFANT_DE both directions and PERE_DE forward have no authored claim -- disclosed corpus coverage gap), 7 excluded_no_parse, 2 excluded_parsing_mismatch. m7_mixed_corpus_promotion_2026-09-18: Answers the load-bearing question raised before choosing the next M7 step (over length>1 extension or third-party validation): does feeding M7's LLM evidence into the SAME M6 promotion pipeline as the adversarial-corpus evidence help, hurt, or leave holdout calibration unchanged? m7_corpus_mixed_v0_1.py unions m6_corpus_from_m4_m5_v0_2.build_real_corpus_v2() (26 records, GROUNDED_DIRECT) with m7_corpus_from_llm_v0_1.build_llm_witnessed_corpus() (16 records, GROUNDED_ANALOGY, all still 16/16 CONTRADICTED as in the 2026-09-17 result) into one combined corpus fed unchanged through split_by_rule/StructuralLearningPolicy/evaluate_promotion. Fairness verified: the LLM mechanism can only add records for rules already present in the adversarial corpus, so split_by_rule assigns the identical holdout rule set under the same seed in both runs -- a genuine same-holdout comparison. Real result (llama3.2:latest, seed=0, brier_threshold=0.5): baseline (adversarial only) holdout Brier=0.48125/ECE=0.025, train=16/holdout=5, PROMOTE; mixed (adversarial+LLM) holdout Brier=0.47/ECE=0.025, train=25/holdout=8, PROMOTE. Honest reading: the Brier movement (0.48125->0.47) is small on a 5-8 record holdout and cannot be credited to genuine LLM analogical skill given its evidence is itself systematically CONTRADICTED regardless of ground truth -- conclusion is calibration-NEUTRAL at current scale/model, not a demonstrated improvement, and does not yet justify further investment (length>1 extension, third-party validation) ahead of improving the LLM's individual accuracy or growing the corpus. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md Sec.6. 364/364 tests passing, zero regression.
